researchQuestion: Do time-aligned disagreements between equity and credit markets contain incremental information, and which market leads under which information/liquidity state?
mechanism: Equity and debt are claims on the same enterprise but differ in payoff convexity, seniority, liquidity and investor base; the same news can therefore transmit at different speed and magnitude.
Credit can react to downside/default information that has limited effect on equity during normal states, while equity can lead when bond trading is sparse or rating/credit data update slowly.
Divergence is a relational state, not a standalone directional prediction.

evidenceAndCounterevidence.support: Some credit-curve research finds CDS/bond term-structure information predicts future firm outcomes or equity returns.
evidenceAndCounterevidence.counter: Multiple studies find stock returns lead corporate bond/CDS returns in firm-specific information, especially where bond trading is less liquid.

evidenceAndCounterevidence.support: CDS and bond markets can contribute unique information around rating events.
evidenceAndCounterevidence.counter: Post-crisis information flow can be bidirectional and regime-dependent.

evidenceAndCounterevidence.support: Credit deterioration with stable equity can be an early-warning hypothesis.
evidenceAndCounterevidence.counter: It can also be a liquidity/technical artifact or a duration/benchmark-matching error rather than true credit leadership.

timingContract: Align equity, bond/CDS/reference observations to the same information cutoff; after-hours rating or overseas-market closes require session-aware knownAt handling.
Do not compare a stale bond mark with a live equity close without carrying staleness explicitly.
Corporate actions, dividends, equity issuance, buybacks and conversions require D11-adjusted event clocks.
Bond optionality/duration/currency and equity corporate-action adjustments must be harmonized before divergence is computed.
falsificationGates: Credit leads equity is not a default assumption; direction must be estimated by state/market and can reverse.
Common macro/liquidity shocks can create apparent lead-lag without issuer-specific information.
Sparse bond trading can manufacture false credit stability or sudden catch-up moves.
Rating lag can make agency-based credit variables appear to follow equity mechanically.
Equity leverage/optionality can create asymmetric reactions unrelated to new credit information.
If divergence adds no residual information after D22-06 spread, D22-05 rating, D13 macro and D04/D05 liquidity controls, classify REJECTED_OR_REDUNDANT.
